purpose: Literature-grounded calibration states for retained-state engineering. Missing values are null rather than inferred.

source.title: Ambient-pressure 151-K superconductivity in HgBa2Ca2Cu3O8+δ via pressure quench

retained_state.structural_support: Synchrotron XRD on pressure-quenched Hg1223 supports a retained strained/defected state, but the atlas does not assume every structural measurement is from the identical 151 K specimen.

retention_observations.note: A pressure-quenched phase with Tc=149 K was reported retained inside the DAC for at least 3 days.
The reported pressure-quenched state remained stable through cycling up to about 170 K, with slight loss of retained Tc.
Cycling to room temperature reduced a retained ambient-pressure Tc from 147 K to 143 K; this is degradation, not a sharp universal failure temperature.

limitations: Retention kinetics are not reduced to a single activation barrier by the source.
Do not generalize the 151 K result to room-temperature storage stability.
Post-quench bulk magnetic confirmation is not encoded here unless explicitly tied to the retained state.

source.title: Ambient pressure recovery of the structurally unconventional hydride Y3Fe4H20

preparation.route: laser-heated DAC synthesis followed by room-temperature decompression

retained_state.structural_support: Single-crystal XRD followed the orthorhombic Cmcm phase during decompression to ambient pressure.

retention_observations.note: XRD established ambient-pressure metastability for about 30 hours in one run.
Recovered samples examined after about one to three months showed a 7–8% volume reduction attributed to hydrogen desorption.

limitations: The material is reported metallic but non-superconducting.
Month-scale observations indicate structural persistence can coexist with continuing hydrogen loss.
60 GPa is the lowest synthesis pressure reported for emergence of the phase, not a universal formation threshold.

source.title: High-Pressure Synthesis of Metastable Superhydride PdH3 by Using Amorphous Pd as a Starting Material

preparation.route: ~2000 K high-pressure synthesis followed by unloading

retained_state.structural_support: The high-pressure PdH3 product was not retained as PdH3; unloading produced PdH1.3.

retention_observations.note: After unloading to ambient conditions the reported recovered composition was PdH1.3.

limitations: This is a pathway/precursor calibration, not evidence for retained PdH3 superconductivity.
The source demonstrates that amorphous and crystalline Pd precursors follow different hydride pathways.

source.title: High-Pressure Synthesis of Metastable Superhydride PdH3 by Using Amorphous Pd as a Starting Material

preparation.route: ~2000 K high-pressure control synthesis followed by unloading

retained_state.structural_support: Crystalline precursor produced Pd3H5 under high pressure and PdH0.706 after quenching to ambient conditions.

retention_observations.note: Recovered composition was reported as PdH0.706 rather than the amorphous-precursor PdH1.3 outcome.

limitations: This is a matched pathway control, not a superconductivity result.
It is included because precursor disorder is itself an experimentally demonstrated state variable.

source.title: Superconducting Hydride Mg2RhH6 Experimentally Achieved at Lower Pressure

preparation.route: two-step H5 precursor to H6 octahedral hydride via additional hydrogen insertion

retained_state.structural_support: The source reports synthesis/structure characterization and zero resistance with magnetic-field suppression of Tc.

limitations: No ambient-pressure superconducting state is asserted by this atlas record.
The 30 GPa entry is a formation/operation anchor for Q-MRH6 retention experiments, not a recovered-state claim.
The source reports Tc increasing to 29 K for synthesis at 53 GPa.
